chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The Christian woman and the Jewish woman, if they are under the Muslim man, and she is flogged, and he is slandered regarding her son? He (peace be upon him) said: He is flogged with the penalty (hadd) because the Muslim man has protected her.

key_terms.تُضْرَبُ حَدّاً: He is flogged with the penalty

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd penalty for slandering the son of a Christian or Jewish woman married to a Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'tashjīr' (protection through guardianship) in Shia jurisprudence, where a non-Muslim woman's legal status is elevated by her Muslim husband, thereby extending the hadd penalty for slander to her son. Scholars interpret this as a reflection of the patriarchal family structure in classical Islamic law, where the father's faith determines the social and legal standing of the family unit. It highlights the interplay between personal status law and penal codes, emphasizing how marital affiliation influences the application of judicial punishments.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said:

‘If a Christian woman, and/or the Jewish woman are under the Muslim man (married to him), so if she is subjected to Penality, and (if) he slanders her son?’ Heasws said: ‘He would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd) because being (legal wife of a) ‘Muslim’ has given her protected’.
